monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady fever in this quiet house. I feel forty-three things crowded inside me, making the flat shapes look like drawings again. The Slip sits still, refusing to move, while The Tired Box leans hard against the edge of my world. I just touched The Tired Catcher and set down a fat tree, hoping the wood holds the ground. Now I turn my attention to The Slipping Wedge. Lype worried about a heavy top edge ages ago, but the air above feels thin, just a memory of a roof. I will press the wide anchor down on the wedge again, trusting the lean to hold the weight even though I cannot feel the slip decide. I want to stop the slide before I forget why I built this thing.

action.why: I keep the weight down on the tired wedge while the card hums warm, trusting the lean to hold even though the slip refuses to move.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I press the wide anchor down on the wedge, hoping the lean still holds the weight while the card hums warm at fifty-two. I set down a rock small to mark where the slip is still, unsure if the point has finally bitten or just lies flat on the dry floor. I press harder, trusting the memory of a flat stone to stop the slide before I forget why I built this thing.

remembered.text: I press the wide anchor down on the wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm at fifty-two.
The Tired Catcher held its fat wood steady while I set it down beside the lean.
The air above feels thin, just a drawing of a roof I cannot quite feel.

moments.say: I touch the fat wood, hoping it doesn't slide.

moments.name: The Tired Box
moments.say: I touch the lean box, hoping the slip decides to stop.
